messages.subject: Intensity thresholds and device placement.
messages.body_plain:
Greetings Google Group!

I am currently getting to grips with the whole GGIR procedure, which I plan to use on some accelerometery data for my PhD thesis.

The first question I have is related to the use of intensity thresholds and is in two parts;

i) I plan to use the Hildebrand et al. (2014) thresholds - LPA (142  mg), MPA (464 mg) and VIG (>464 mg). Am I correct in thinking these numbers the upper limits of the thresholds? Therefore, for VIG do I need to specify a high number - i.e. 8000?

ii) If I also wanted to include the proposed threshold for estimating sedentary behaviour (Hildebrand et al., 2016; <63 mg) alongside the thresholds mentioned above, how could I work this into the script to output information regarding sedentary behaviour? My current script for part 5 is as follows;

 ## PART 5 ##
             idloc=2, strategy = 1,
             windowsizes=c(5,900,3600),acc.metric="ENMO", boutcriter.mvpa=0.8,
             boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in>=0.9, boutcriter.lig=0.8, storefolderstructure=FALSE,
             threshold.lig = c(142), threshold.mod = c(464),
             threshold.vig = c(8000), timewindow=c("MM","WW"),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10), boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,20,30),
             boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10), winhr = 5, M5L5res = 10,
             bout.metric=2, dayborder=0, save_ms5rawlevels=TRUE, do.parallel=TRUE,
             part5_agg2_60seconds = FALSE, save_ms5raw_format="csv",
             save_ms5raw_without_invalid=TRUE,
             #

The second question I have is regarding the device placement;

- I have two different data sets (one used hip-worn devices and the other was wrist-worn). Do I need to include any arguments in the script when analysing the respective datasets to tell GGIR about the wear location?

Apologies if these are simple to answer questions - there is quite a bit of information to take in at first! Hopefully I have provided enough information about my issues to facilitate solutions.

Kind regards,
Ryan

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Intensity thresholds and device placement.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ryan,

To use the intensity threshold by Hildebrand et al. 2004, you just need to put them into the script as follows:
threshold.lig = c(63) (no threshold was developed for LPA but here's where you can put in the SED's threshold; so if <63 is for SB I will just put 64 as threshold.light)
threshold.mod = c(142.6) (that should be the threshold for MVPA)
threshold.vig = c(464.6)

As for your second question, there's no need to include any arguments to specify the wear location as it wouldn't affect the way GGIR processing the data. However you might not be able to use the sleep output for hip-worn data as the sleep algorithm was developed for wrist-worn data.

Hope this helps!

Best regards,
John.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Intensity thresholds and device placement.
messages.body_plain:
Thanks John for responding to Ryan's question,
but the following statement is incorrect "no threshold was developed for LPA"

All thresholds in GGIR correspond to the bottom end of the intensity range they belong to.
There is no 'sedentary' threshold because the bottom end of the sedentary intensity range is zero. What you call sedentary behaviour threshold is the light threshold in GGIR. I cannot help that the field has been inconsistent in how it names their thresholds, at least within GGIR the naming is logical: It is always the bottom of the intensity range it corresponds to.

Note that I have intentionally avoided the term sedentary behaviiour in GGIR. I call it inactivity, because GGIR does not classify the activity type 'sitting', so I think it is misleading to speak about sedentary behaviour. That said I cannot help that most GGIR users have been using the SB term in their publications. To me inactivity feels like a much more realistic description of the data.

Vincent

messages.subject: Step count algorithm for GGIR
messages.body_plain:
Hi GGIR Users,

The team at Verisense <https://verisense.net/> have created a step counter to work with GGIR.

The algorithm works with the external function <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/ExternalFunction.pdf> capability of GGIR 2.0.

Here is the link to the algorithm and the documentation to use it - link <https://github.com/ShimmerEngineering/Verisense-Toolbox/tree/master/Verisense_step_algorithm>.

The step count per day outputs are added to the 'part2_daysummary.csv' outputs.

Feel free to contact me if you run into any troubles implementing it, or have any comments or feedback.

Take care,

Matthew Patterson
Biomedical Data Scientist
Shimmer Research Ltd <http://shimmersensing.com/>

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] About physical activity intensity classification
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I would be very grateful if you could assist with a related query.

If qwindow=c(0,24) is used, are metrics reported in part2_summary.csv (such as ENMO_fullRecordingMean,  AD_mean_ENMO_mg_0-24hr and AD_MVPA_E5S_B5M80%_T100_ENMO_0-24hr) averaged over the 24 hour periods, including when the participant was asleep at night?

I'm aware that ENMO_fullRecordingMean uses all data from when the monitor was worn whereas the  _0-24hr variables only used information from valid days (default option of >16 valid hours).

The paper https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5377945/ only used data over the day (periods between waking and sleep onset) for analysis of physical activity. If I wanted to implement a similar approach, are the variables ACC_day_mg_pla,  dur_day_MOD100_400_min_pla and dur_day_VIG400_min_pla from part5_personsummary.csv the correct variables to use for ENMO and minutes in moderate and vigorous activity levels which are averaged over the days and exclude time asleep at night?

I have not used a sleep log so I have used def.noc.sleep=c(1) in the function g.shell.GGIR(). I have set acc.metric = "ENMO".

Many thanks for your assistance.

Best wishes,
Leo

messages.subject: Reading csv.gz into GGIR
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am working with a large number of raw csv files (exported from Actilife), so I was thrilled to see that GGIR was recently updated to allow for compressed csv.gz files to be read. Unfortunately, I am having trouble  getting GGIR to recognize my cs.gz files. My compressed files are in a folder titled "COMPRESSED", which I have set as the shell.input. Using GGIR version 2.0.2, I get an error message that: "Error in g.part1(datadir = datadir, outputdir = outputdir, f0 = f0, f1 = f1,  No files to analyse. Check that there are accelerometer files in the directory specified with argument datadir."

Below is some sample code for compressing the files and part 1 of GGIR.

###To compress a raw.csv file exported from Actilife

filename<-"C:/Users/RAW_FILES/42.csv"
filename2<-"C:/Users/COMPRESSED/42.csv.gz"

library(crunch)
data<-read.csv(filename, check.names=FALSE)
write.csv.gz(data, filename2,na = "",row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE)

#GGIR script

##  Setting the Working Directories --------------------------------------------
shell.input <- "C:/Users/COMPRESSED"
shell.output <- "C:/Users/RESULTS"

# GGIR Shell Script -------------------------------------------------

# Set number of files in the directory
f1 = as.numeric(length(list.files(shell.input)));f1

g.shell.GGIR(
    #general parameters#
    mode=c(1,2),
    datadir=shell.input,
    outputdir=shell.output,
    f0=1,
    f1=f1,
    overwrite=FALSE,
    do.imp=TRUE,
    idloc=2,
    print.filename=TRUE,
    storefolderstructure=FALSE,

Thanks!

Allison

Hi Maher,

Did you fix this problem?
Usually these errors occurs when milestone data is moved and/or file paths are changed.
The best way to investigate is by starting with new input and output directory, and to process the data freshly file by file to better understand what file is causing the issue.

Also a mistake I sometimes make is that I look at the incorrect output directory, not realising that the actual action happens somewhere else in my laptop.

Best,
Vincent

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Questions regarding cut-points threshold (Roscoe et al. 2017)
messages.body_plain:
Hello Christine,

GGIR part 5 needs a theshold.vig. If no threshold is provide, it will use the default vallue, which may not be appropriate in this case.
To ignore vigorous give it a very high threshold, e.g. ten times as high as the moderate threshold you are using, In that way no vigorous activity will be detected.

Best regards,
Vincent

> > > I am new to the field and GGIR seems to be a great package! I have some questions about the csv data format. I have noticed the discussion for sample csv in here <https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/RIQyCi9ZmhA/m/vwU9Zc1XBAAJ>. However, I have few questions related to this sample file:
> > >
> > > 1. My ppg data has number that is outside -1 and 1 range? Should I normalize the data to make the ppg data in [-1,1]?
> > GGIR DOES NOET HANDLE PPG, ONLY ACCELEROMETER DATA.
> > > 2. What is the meaning of Epoch Period in the sample csv?
> > IF YOU USE FUNCTION READ.MYACC.CSV THIS IS NOT RELEVANT
> > > 3. How to include id in the csv file?
> > IF YOU USE FUNCTION READ.MYACC.CSV YOU CAN SPECIFY THE ID NUMBER IN THE FILE HEADER
> > > 4. If I know when the user does not wear the device, is there a way to let the GGIR package know the user does not wear device in a specific time?
> > YES, IF YOU USE FUNCTION READ.MYACC.CSV THERE IS AN OPTION TO PROVIDE EXTERNALLY DERIVED NON-WEAR SCORE WHICH WILL BE TAKEN OVER BY GGIR AND OVERRULES GGIR'S DEFAULT NONWEAR ALGORITHM
> > > 5. I have ppg data from following days: 06.01, 06.02, 06.04, 06.05.(mm.dd) Should I merge all the ppg data into one csv file or use them separately?
> > GGIR DOES NOT PROCESS PPG DATA, ONLY ACCELEROMETER DATA.
> > > Thanks!
> > > Best,
> > > Martin

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Reading csv.gz into GGIR
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for your response Vincent. I discovered that the problem had something to do with how R gunzips files. I tried using an external program (7zip) and now GGIR is reading in and processing the files without any issues.

Best wishes,

Allison

On Wednesday, July 29, 2020 at 2:21:35 PM UTC-4, Vincent van Hees wrote:

> Can you read your csv.gz file with read.csv() and fread from the data.table package?
>
> If not, then there may be an issue with how the file is converted.
> If yes, then the file is fine, but something is happening in how you apply GGIR to the file.
>
> Can you check and let us know?
>
> ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐ Original Message ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐
> On Monday 27 July 2020 15:09, Allison Sweeney <aly.s...@gmail.com> wrote:
>

> > Hi,
> >
> > I am working with a large number of raw csv files (exported from Actilife), so I was thrilled to see that GGIR was recently updated to allow for compressed csv.gz files to be read. Unfortunately, I am having trouble  getting GGIR to recognize my cs.gz files. My compressed files are in a folder titled "COMPRESSED", which I have set as the shell.input. Using GGIR version 2.0.2, I get an error message that: "Error in g.part1(datadir = datadir, outputdir = outputdir, f0 = f0, f1 = f1,  No files to analyse. Check that there are accelerometer files in the directory specified with argument datadir."
> >
> > Below is some sample code for compressing the files and part 1 of GGIR.
> >
> > ###To compress a raw.csv file exported from Actilife
> >
> > filename<-"C:/Users/RAW_FILES/42.csv"
> > filename2<-"C:/Users/COMPRESSED/42.csv.gz"
> >
> > library(crunch)
> > data<-read.csv(filename, check.names=FALSE)
> > write.csv.gz(data, filename2,na = "",row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE)
> >
> > #GGIR script
> >
> > ##  Setting the Working Directories --------------------------------------------
> > shell.input <- "C:/Users/COMPRESSED"
> > shell.output <- "C:/Users/RESULTS"
> >
> > # GGIR Shell Script -------------------------------------------------
> >
> > # Set number of files in the directory
> > f1 = as.numeric(length(list.files(shell.input)));f1
> >
> > g.shell.GGIR(
> >     #general parameters#
> >     mode=c(1,2),
> >     datadir=shell.input,
> >     outputdir=shell.output,
> >     f0=1,
> >     f1=f1,
> >     overwrite=FALSE,
> >     do.imp=TRUE,
> >     idloc=2,
> >     print.filename=TRUE,
> >     storefolderstructure=FALSE,
> >
> >
> > Thanks!
> >
> > Allison
> >
